title: U.S. House · Mississippi's 3rd District
area: Central Mississippi, including parts of the Jackson metro area, Meridian, Brookhaven, and Starkville

context.text: Michael Guest ran unopposed in the March 10, 2026 Republican primary. Michael Chiaradio ran unopposed for the Democratic nomination. Shaun McInnish Sr. did not make the Libertarian ballot; Erik Kiehle is the Libertarian nominee.

candidates.name: Michael Guest
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the March 10, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Michael Guest has represented Mississippi's 3rd Congressional District since 2019. A Rankin County resident, he was a prosecutor in Madison and Rankin counties for more than a decade and was elected district attorney there in 2007. In the 119th Congress he chairs the House Committee on Ethics and the Homeland Security Committee's Border Security and Enforcement subcommittee and sits on Appropriations.

background.text: A Rankin County resident and graduate of Brandon High School, according to his official biography.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Mississippi State University (1992) and a J.D. from the University of Mississippi (1995).
Served as an assistant district attorney for Madison and Rankin counties from 1995 to 2007.
Was elected district attorney of Madison and Rankin counties in 2007.
Won the 2018 general election, defeating Michael Evans (D), to succeed retiring Rep. Gregg Harper (R).
His official biography says he was the first Republican freshman in the 116th Congress to pass a bill, the Terrorist and Foreign Fighter Travel Exercise Act of 2019, which was signed into law.
Chairs the House Committee on Ethics in the 119th Congress.

Chairs the Border Security and Enforcement subcommittee of the House Committee on Homeland Security and sits on the House Committee on Appropriations, including its Homeland Security, Energy and Water Development, and Military Construction-Veterans Affairs subcommittees.

According to his official biography, he is a member of the Rankin County Bar Association and the Mississippi Bar Association, teaches a Sunday school class at Brandon Baptist Church, and is married with two sons.

priorities.text: Describes himself as a conservative who supports limited government, lower taxes and fewer regulations, a strong national defense, and Second Amendment gun rights.
As chairman of the Border Security and Enforcement Subcommittee, focuses on securing the U.S.-Mexico border.

positions.summary: Describes himself as supporting the right to life of the unborn and has been recognized by Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America and the Family Research Council for his pro-life record.
positions.quote: the right to life of the unborn

positions.summary: Describes himself as supporting Second Amendment gun rights and has been recognized by the National Rifle Association for his defense of gun rights.

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Ethics in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Chairs the Border Security and Enforcement subcommittee of the House Homeland Security Committee in the 119th Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Guest has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. His official House issues page has no topic subpages; positions above are drawn from his official 'About' biography page. His committee chairmanship of Border Security and Enforcement points to a focus on border security, but the page's language ('secure our border') does not itself call for expanded enforcement or deportations, so no immigration_enforcement position was added. Key floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Michael Chiaradio
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed for the March 10, 2026 Democratic nomination

summary.text: Michael Chiaradio is a Democrat who owns a regenerative farm in Shubuta, Mississippi. Originally from Teaneck, New Jersey, he played professional baseball, started small businesses including a women's softball league, and spent nearly four years in leadership at the government contractor Maximus Inc. He says he is running on investing in people, agriculture, and healthcare.

background.text: Born and raised in Teaneck, New Jersey, and graduated from Teaneck High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Eastern Nazarene College (2013) and an MBA from Felician University (2021).
Says he played college baseball and then in the inaugural season of what became the Empire Professional Baseball League, and worked in league operations afterward.
Launched small businesses, most notably a professional softball league, the American Softball Association (ASBA Softball), in Satsuma, Alabama, which he says ran for two summers.
Spent nearly four years in leadership at Maximus Inc., a global government contractor that supports Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act.
Lives in Shubuta, Mississippi, where he owns and operates a regenerative farm.
Was the only candidate in the March 10, 2026 Democratic primary for the 3rd District.

priorities.text: "Investing in Our People": says simply raising taxes or cutting spending does not solve economic problems and calls for better-targeted government spending.
priorities.quote: Investing in Our People: Simply raising taxes or cutting spending does not solve our economic problems. We need BETTER spending that invests in our people.

priorities.text: "America's Competitive Advantages": wants investment in agriculture and healthcare as foundational U.S. economic strengths.
"North American Production": favors growing North American manufacturing and trade cooperation rather than competing alone in global markets.

positions.summary: Lists healthcare access and affordability among his passionate policy areas, drawing on his background working with Medicaid/ACA-related government contracting.

summary.text: Erik Kiehle is a property manager and the Libertarian nominee in the 3rd District. He holds a bachelor's degree from the University of California, Riverside. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes his candidacy as an alternative to the Democratic and Republican parties and lists balancing the budget as a key message.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of California, Riverside (1994).
Works as a property manager.
Says his first job was at Baskin-Robbins during high school and summer college breaks.
Is the Libertarian candidate on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot for the 3rd District.

priorities.text: Says he will vote against spending bills that add to the federal debt and wants a constitutional amendment requiring balanced budgets.
priorities.quote: End deficit spending and balance the budget. I will vote AGAINST spending bills that add to the federal debt and will push for a Constitutional Amendment to require balanced budgets

priorities.text: Wants to end U.S. spending related to the wars in Ukraine and Iran and end all U.S. aid to Israel.
Supports mass deportations and a ban on immigration from Muslim-majority countries.

positions.summary: Candidate Connection survey states he wants to end all U.S. aid to Israel and calls for declaring Israel a national security threat.
Survey lists mass deportations as a top priority.
